selection.rationale: Objective is ttft_ms, whose frozen boundary (qwen_inference.py infer / opop_adapter.run) is exactly the prefill phase: synchronize, model(input_ids=[1,256], use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1), first argmax, synchronize. Measured evidence: independently measured original baseline ttft_ms=25.279672; the execution_timeline diagnostic records 2146 CUDA kernels inside the prefill window with an active union of 21.39 ms, so roughly 3.9 ms of the clean TTFT window is non-GPU time (host dispatch of ~2146 kernel submissions across 545 module invocations, tail drain, select/argmax, sync). Corroborating host evidence: python_runtime cProfile (perturbing, non-scoring) shows per-op Python dispatch dominating self time (torch linear builtin 8096 calls/106 ms self, Tensor.to 85 ms, RMSNorm forward 140.7 ms self over 4640 calls); device_telemetry samples GPU utilization at only 11-48% during workload windows. Prefill CUDA composition (nested diagnostic) is 16.43 ms aten::linear across 253 site-calls plus ~2.6 ms of RMSNorm decomposed into ~730 tiny mean/pow/add/rsqrt/mul kernels and ~0.7 ms SDPA - a dispatch-dense, GEMM-dominated region whose wall time is bounded below by its ~21.4 ms GPU-active floor. The editable boundary chosen is the whole prefill bundle: the Qwen3ForCausalLM prefill module call 900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a (group e0861b46dbeeb562f67f) and all 3642 observed calls strictly beneath it (670 groups, all of whose calls lie inside the region; the anchor call executes once per run with fixed [1,256] input). The select+argmax after the forward live in the frozen adapter loop and stay eager and untouched; the 31 decode steps stay on the source eager path with all their hooks, so inherited decode coverage is unaffected. Six mixed-phase groups whose call sites are shared with decode (798df708d05932b17f71, d77c0c4f92011fcbd64b, 500ee891ce2ab44a5d67, a6a04d83b5d1f2b1435b, 9e7a0a6648205712c565, 4f4d1328a28633696964) are deliberately not selected as groups - only their prefill-member call IDs are listed in affected_calls - so no decode call is claimed as affected. Per the binding contract, subsuming the prefill children requires explicitly replacing the whole bundle, which this region selection does; the replacement anchors at the module boundary and consumes the current parent via context.references rather than re-deriving original work.
selection.hypothesis: Replace the prefill bundle with a lazily built CUDA-graph execution of the accepted parent work: on the first real adapter invocation (inside torch.inference_mode and the active phase context), copy the static [1,256] input into a static buffer, call the current callable at the e0861b46dbeeb562f67f boundary through context.references under torch.cuda.graph capture, keep static logits and static past_key_values output buffers, then on every subsequent run copy current inputs in, replay, and hand the graph-written K/V tensors to the eager decode loop via a request-local DynamicCache wrapper. Replay executes the identical kernels in identical order on current inputs each invocation, so tokens/logits are bit-identical to the parent implementation while per-kernel host dispatch (2146 submissions, 545 module wrappers, RMSNorm/rotary op-by-op launches) leaves the TTFT critical path. Testable prediction: ttft_ms drops from 25.28 ms toward the ~21.4-22.0 ms GPU-active floor, i.e. about 3-4 ms (~12-15%), with decode_ms, tokens and logits unchanged; if the clean-run gap is already overlapped, the measured gain shrinks toward zero and the fallback inside the same region is dispatch-reducing fusion (packed q/k/v and gate/up GEMMs, fused RMSNorm) which trades bit-exactness for tolerance-bounded numerics. Unknowns kept explicit: GPU model and GEMM headroom are not identified in the evidence, the 3.9 ms clean-gap is inferred from baseline wall minus diagnostic GPU union across separate captures, and graph private-pool memory overhead is unmeasured but bounded by the prefill transient footprint against the 8.24 GB reserved baseline.

proposal.rationale: Objective is ttft_ms only (paired, minimize). Measured evidence: the original baseline ttft_ms is 25.28 while the prefill-phase CUDA kernel sum inside the same boundary is 21.53 ms (target-resources.json root project call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0, phase_cuda_us.prefill), i.e. ~3.7 ms of the TTFT window is host launch/dispatch gap across the ~600 prefill kernels (36 decoder layers x GEMM/norm/RoPE/SDPA chains). python_runtime observations corroborate host-bound dispatch (nn.Module._call_impl cumulative 959 ms over one 32-step workload). The selected site is the prefill-phase call of the root Qwen3ForCausalLM module (call 900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a, target 'model'), whose observed signature is exactly the adapter's prefill call kwargs {input_ids [1,256] int64 cuda, use_cache: true, logits_to_keep: 1}. The replacement lazily captures the UNCHANGED parent forward into a single CUDA graph during the first actual adapter invocation (build/installation never calls the parent; capture happens while the evaluator's installed dispatch and the adapter's phase context are live, so the recorded work is the accepted parent's work), then on every invocation copies the current input_ids into the static input buffer and replays the graph. The workload therefore executes on the live inputs on every invocation (no fixture outputs are captured; only the operation graph), and the replayed kernel sequence is exactly the parent's, so logits and greedy tokens are expected to be bitwise identical to the reference (quality: logits atol/rtol 0.02, exact greedy tokens). This collapses per-kernel launch gaps and removes Python dispatch inside prefill: expected ttft ~21.6-22.2 ms vs 25.28 ms (~12-15% reduction), far above the MAD-derived noise bound. Decode is deliberately untouched: the framework's phase guard routes the decode-phase calls to the parent forward, and decode consumes the returned cache wrapper (a transformers DynamicCache-semantics view whose layer objects are rebound to the graph's static KV pool buffers at each prefill; decode's DynamicCache.update appends eagerly exactly as with the parent's cache). No distributed mechanism is involved (communication not_applicable for this single-device task). inputs/previous-feedback.txt and inputs/previous-candidate/ are absent, so this is a first attempt with no prior attempt feedback to incorporate. project.invoke is outside the supplied selection closure (selection.affected_calls contains only the 3642 module/functional prefill sites), so the whole-prefill execution policy is implemented at the root module site that contains every descendant prefill call; inner sites are not eliminated - their native kernels still execute inside the replayed graph each invocation.
proposal.setup_work: Installation (build) allocates nothing and calls no parent code; it only constructs the engine closure. On the first actual invocation of the installed replacement (an untimed quality-mode step, before any measured repeat): (1) two warmup parent prefill forwards on a private side stream (~2 x 22 ms GPU, each creating and discarding its own DynamicCache); (2) one CUDA graph capture pass recording the unchanged parent forward with a static clone of the current input_ids (capture does not execute kernels; torch.cuda.graph entry also performs a one-time synchronize/empty_cache); (3) an immediate replay produces that invocation's real output. Every later invocation does only: guard checks, a 2 KB input_ids copy_ into the static buffer, one graph replay, and a pure-Python rebinding of the 36 cache layer objects to the static KV pool tensors (no kernels). Setup allocation/retention: the CUDA graph's private memory pool retains the prefill KV buffers (~37.7 MB bf16 for 36 layers x GQA 8 kv heads x 256 tokens x 128 head_dim) plus the capture-time activation high-water mark (expected on the order of 100-300 MB, exact figure unmeasured here) and the static ids/logits buffers (<1 MB). Expect framework.reserved_bytes and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes to increase by that retained pool, while per-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes can decrease because prefill intermediates are allocated inside the graph pool rather than the run-time allocator; these counter moves are allocator-scope effects, not general physical-memory savings. No batch, sequence-length, token-count, sampling, data, dtype or threshold changes.
quality_risks: Numerical: the replayed kernel sequence is captured from the unchanged parent on the same shapes/stream, so logits/tokens are expected bitwise identical to the eager reference; cuBLAS run-to-run nondeterminism between capture and later replays on identical inputs is not expected on a fixed device/driver, but if any divergence appeared it would surface as a quality-check failure, not silently pass.

CUDA Graph capture may be unsupported in a specific diagnostic context (torch.profiler/kineto active, e.g. discovery re-capture or execution_timeline): the engine detects an active profiler and permanently routes to the parent (route 'setup_failure_profiler_active'), so those diagnostic runs observe the eager parent prefill; clean quality/measure runs are unaffected.

Any exception during warmup/capture ('setup_failure_capture') or during replay ('runtime_failure_fallback_parent') permanently disables the graph path and falls back to the parent callable for that and later calls; the candidate then behaves exactly like the parent (no improvement, no quality change).

Signature guard: only the observed prefill signature (kwargs-only input_ids int64 cuda 2-D, use_cache True, logits_to_keep 1, no attention_mask/position_ids/past_key_values/inputs_embeds/labels, shape equal to the captured shape) takes the graph path; every other call (including all decode-phase calls, which are additionally blocked by the framework phase guard) goes to the parent.

State/alias semantics: the returned output reuses the captured ModelOutput object; its logits tensor aliases the graph's static pool buffer (the adapter only slices/argmaxes/stacks it within the same invocation and observe() clones it), and past_key_values is a fresh-per-prefill cache view over the same static KV pool buffers, rebuilt by pure-Python layer rebinding each invocation so decode appends can never leak across invocations; weights, RNG and global math policies are untouched.

Memory counters: retained graph pool increases reserved/lifecycle-reserved peaks as described in setup_work; this is reported setup allocation, not hidden by any measurement-boundary change (TTFT/decode boundaries keep the source's synchronize structure).
